transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-12-29 10:30 PST | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ivy Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Duarte (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connell (Aurora Head Partnerships), Priya Nair (Aurora Solutions Architect), Eric Zhao (Aurora VP Product)

Summary (auto): quick intro, high level use cases, infra constraints, agree to tech deep dive and send deck

00:00 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ivy from Redwood, AE on this account, um we'll do quick intros. Rafael's our solutions engineer. Maya is on CSM. How are you folks?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): Hey Ivy, thanks. Liam here, head of cloud partnerships at Aurora. We've got Priya and Eric on the call. Appreciate the time.
00:22 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Nice to meet you. Quick agenda — learn about Aurora's partner offerings, see where Redwood might fit, discuss tech and security requirements, and propose next steps.
00:35 Speaker 4 (Priya): Sounds good. Quick context — Aurora runs managed GPU clusters across EU and NA, we also have on-prem appliances for telco customers. We're exploring partners for inference stack and routing options.
01:05 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Okay great, are you mostly targeting enterprise customers for inference workloads or a mix of SaaS partners?
01:14 Speaker 4 (Priya): Mostly enterprise — finance, healthcare, and a few gaming workloads. Data residency is often required, so VPC or on-prem variants are common asks. Also latency sensitive for some gaming partners.
01:40 Speaker 2 (Liam): To add, we're interested in both being a reseller and a technical integration partner — e.g., Aurora could offer Redwood Dedicated as a packaged offering on our infra.
02:03 Speaker 3 (Rafael): That aligns with what we do — Redwood Dedicated can be run on reserved GPU pools, with configurable autoscaling and SLA. We also have Redwood Private for VPC or air-gapped deployments. Sometimes folks call it Redwood Privet in transcripts, haha.
02:30 Speaker 5 (Eric): What's the typical onboarding time for Dedicated on a partner's infra? Do you need changes to our provisioning tooling?
02:42 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Usually 4–8 weeks for an initial integration and pilot, depending on network and onboarding. We integrate with your cluster scheduler and provisioning APIs, and we support common orchestration systems. There's a short checklist: network routes, certs, KMS integration, and optional HSM.
03:10 Speaker 2 (Liam): Security is big for our enterprise customers — SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML, audit logs. Can Redwood support those out of the box?
03:22 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Yes, we have SOC2 attestation, SAML-based SSO, RBAC, audit trails, and KMS integrations. For air-gapped installs we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll share the security pack — note: sometimes the doc labels are a bit messy but we'll send the right one.
03:49 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Quick qual question — what models do your customers run? Are they mostly open models, LLMs like Llama derivatives, or proprietary models?
04:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): A bit of everything. Finance tends to run fine-tuned Llama/Alpaca variants, healthcare sometimes uses smaller domain-specific models, and gaming folks experiment with larger open LMs. We also see customers wanting GPU-accelerated embeddings.
04:32 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Good, our runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths, KV cache, continuous batching — though we've seen people mis-hear KV cache as K V cash in notes — but the short is we can optimize cost with smart batching and caching.
04:55 Speaker 5 (Eric): On billing and go-to-market, how does partnership typically work? Resell? Marketplace listing?
05:06 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Both. We have marketplace integrations and reseller agreements. For Dedicated, partners can bundle a managed offering with reserved capacity and split revenue; for Redwood Hosted we can offer referral credits. We'll share a partnership one-pager.
05:28 Speaker 2 (Liam): Good. On the technical side, Priya, can you share Aurora's typical GPU instance types and network topology?
05:36 Speaker 4 (Priya): We run a mix: A100s for large models, H100s in select regions, and some T4s for lightweight inference. Networking is VPC peering or private interconnect for larger enterprise customers.
06:02 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Perfect. One area to clarify — for model variants and fallbacks we support smart routing (latency/cost/region) and automatic fallback to quantized variants if capacity constrained.
06:18 Speaker 5 (Eric): Any performance benchmarks you'd like us to run? Sequence lengths, throughput targets?
06:25 Speaker 3 (Rafael): For a pilot, reasonable targets are 99th percentile latency under Xms for 2k tokens — but we usually calibrate per model. We'll propose a benchmark plan: sample prompts, sequence lengths, and target SLOs. We'll also do a cost-per-token estimate with and without batching.
06:50 Speaker 4 (Priya): That sounds fair. Security — we'd need to map out audit log requirements and data retention. How detailed is Redwood's audit logging?
07:02 Speaker 3 (Rafael): It's token-level and per-route tracing hooks; we can provide per-request metadata and long-term export to your SIEM. We support configurable retention windows.
07:18 Speaker 1 (Ivy): One common objection we hear is latency vs cost — folks worry dedicated is expensive. We usually show numbers from Redwood Optimize where batching and quantization reduce unit cost without big latency penalties.
07:40 Speaker 4 (Priya): Are you able to run inference on-prem for customers who won't allow any cloud egress?
07:48 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem packaged installs; there are added ops requirements and a longer lead time. We can do air-gapped installs and integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
08:05 Speaker 2 (Liam): On compliance paperwork, can we get a copy of your SOC2 and ISO certs? Also need to see your standard MSA for reselling.
08:16 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Absolutely — I'll attach the security pack and redwood reseller MSA. We'll include contact info for our compliance team.
08:30 Speaker 5 (Eric): For initial commercial structure — are you proposing revenue share or referral? Our GTM prefers revenue share for managed offerings.
08:42 Speaker 1 (Ivy): We can be flexible; usually for Dedicated bundled with partner infra we do a revenue share, and for hosted we do referral/credit models. We'll draft a sample MOU.
09:01 Speaker 4 (Priya): For the tech deep dive, who from Redwood should participate? We might want infra and networking people from Aurora there.
09:10 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Rafael (SE) will lead the technical deep dive; we should invite our infra integration engineer and maybe an SRE familiar with KV cache and batching. It would be helpful to have Aurora's network and security leads.
09:28 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Timing wise, what's your target to have a pilot live?
09:33 Speaker 2 (Liam): Ideally Q1 — Jan/Feb — but flexible. If we can lock a small pilot by mid-Feb we can present at our partner summit in March.
09:48 Speaker 3 (Rafael): That is doable; we'll target a Jan tech deep dive and aim for a Feb pilot kickoff. We'll create a milestones spreadsheet.
10:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): What about support SLAs for production workloads? Nbd if you have tiers but we need to know response times.
10:12 Speaker 1 (Ivy): We have tiered support; enterprise customers can opt into 24/7 support and faster incident SLAs. For Dedicated there's an SLA-backed latency and uptime target.
10:30 Speaker 5 (Eric): A few quick clarifying questions about integration: does Redwood require any kernel-level changes or special drivers on our nodes?
10:40 Speaker 3 (Rafael): No kernel changes — we use standard drivers and optimized kernels but they run in user-space. We'll provide a compatibility matrix. Sometimes folks mis-label MPS vs our continuous batching — but we'll clarify.
11:05 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Great. Any other objections or concerns from Aurora side?
11:12 Speaker 4 (Priya): Mainly around data residency, audit logs, and operational burden — we need to ensure it's low for Aurora's managed offering.
11:25 Speaker 3 (Rafael): Understood. For pilot we can limit scope: single region, defined model set, and monitoring hooks so operational load is bounded.
11:40 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Recap and next steps: I'll send the partner deck, MSA draft, and security pack. Rafael will propose times for technical deep dive and initial benchmark plan. Priya will share GPU inventory and network topology. Liam will loop in commercial terms.
12:05 Speaker 2 (Liam): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
12:10 Speaker 1 (Ivy): Thanks — we'll follow up in email with calendar invites. Linking the partner deck here: https://redwood.example.com/decks/aurora-partner-deck.pdf

Auto items:
Action items captured inline. Agreed pilot timeline: tech deep dive in early Jan, pilot targeted for Feb.

End of transcript.
